T he third edition of the Lagos International Theatre Festival attracted over 20,000 attendees, featuring more than 25 productions and international performances from four countries. The seven-day festival, held from November 9 to 15, brought together Nigerian and international theatre practitioners, creatives, diplomats and cultural enthusiasts, further strengthening Lagos’ position as a growing destination for theatre and the performing arts. The festival opened with Theatre Meets Food at Kaly Restaurant, featuring celebrity chef Hilda Baci in a fusion of culinary artistry and live performance. Speaking on the success of the festival, its Founder and Creative Producer, Bolanle Austen-Peters, said the vision was to establish a platform that would give African stories greater international recognition. “Our ambition has always been to create more than a theatre festival. We want to build a platform that places Lagos firmly on the global cultural map, gives African stories the international visibility they deserve and creates meaningful opportunities for our artists,” she said. Add us to your Preferred Sources Austen-Peters added that the turnout and international participation affirmed the festival’s vision, noting, “Theatre is not just entertainment; it is an instrument of cultural identity, economic opportunity and global influence.” The festival featured performances from Kenya, Brazil, Norway and Canada, alongside diplomatic engagements, cultural exchanges and networking opportunities aimed at promoting collaboration within the global creative industry. Other activities included diplomatic and cultural engagements hosted by the United States Consul General in Lagos and the British Embassy. The British Council also organised a networking reception for festival directors and participating production companies. Among those in attendance were Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu; the Chargé d’Affaires of the US Mission in Nigeria; the US Consul General, Brandon Hudspeth; the British Deputy High Commissioner; and representatives of the Brazilian, South African and South Korean diplomatic missions. Sanwo-Olu received an award in recognition of his support for the arts, while veteran theatre practitioner, Ben Tomoloju, was honoured with a Lifetime Achievement and Legacy Award for his contributions to the development of the arts in Nigeria. The main performance programme took place from November 14 to 15 across the MUSON Centre, Ouida and KAP Hub, featuring more than 25 productions by established and emerging Nigerian creatives, as well as international performers. The Festival Director, Vanessa Jev, described the achievement as a product of artistic vision, partnerships and collective commitment. “We are proud to have created a platform where Nigerian and international artists could share their work, connect with new audiences and build lasting relationships,” she said. Jev added that the success would provide a stronger foundation for expanding the festival’s reach and creating more opportunities for the creative community. The festival was supported by sponsors and partners, including Afreximbank, Waltersmith, Pillar Oil, MTN, Wema Bank, the United States Consulate, British Council and Channels Television, among others.
